agents.role: Runs the patrol loop over the watched hosts and the public vulnerability feed. It observes and records machine states; it never changes, patches, restarts, or reconfigures anything it watches.
Appends every patrol observation to the patrol record and keeps the seen-state, so the record of what was actually observed is complete and checkable afterward.

The only agent in this pack that may post across worlds. On a red patrol it runs the escalation chain to the labelled SIMULATED endpoint and sends summary counts (never hostnames) to the ops room; it never contacts a real responder, vendor, or service.

alerts.carries: The watched host label, the certificate's expiry date, and the whole days remaining. Local only; the record names the state, never a cause.
The watched host label and the certificate's expiry date, which is in the past. Local only.

The CVE id, the matched inventory entry (vendor and product as configured), and the feed's listing date. Local only; presence means the configured inventory names the product, not that an exploit was observed.
The watched host label, the port checked, and the observation time. Local only; down means the patrol's check failed, stated as an observation, never a diagnosis.
The watched host label and the sensitive port that answered without being declared expected. Local only.
Counts only: how many red observations of each category the patrol recorded, and the patrol timestamp. Never hostnames, addresses, certificate details, or vulnerability detail.

sends.carries: Red observation counts by category and the patrol timestamp. Counts only.
never_carries: hostnames or IP addresses of watched machines

firstboot.label: Hosts to watch: hostname, service port, and the ports declared expected-open for each
Software inventory to match against the known-exploited-vulnerability feed: vendor and product names as the feed lists them
Days before expiry at which a certificate counts as expiring

pack_name: Meta Custos machine watch world pack

bus_summary: Red observation counts by category on an escalating patrol
Patrol completion counts: hosts checked, observations by category
local_only: Hostnames and addresses of watched machines
Which inventory entries matched which feed entries
The full patrol record before it is reviewed

parts.proven: Pinning tests on injected signals (tests/custos/): certificate tier boundaries, feed matching against the configured inventory, exposure classification, yellow records produce zero escalation calls, red records escalate only to the labelled SIMULATED endpoint, records append and feed entries are not re-alerted across patrols; a failed certificate probe or an unparseable certificate date is an error in the summary, never data and never a patrol crash. One live stage-1 patrol against the real CISA feed (1,766 entries seen; the example inventory matched 5) is committed under worlds/custos/runs/ — a feed patrol only: the development machine has no direct network path to watched hosts, so host probes are pinned on injected signals, not live ones. UNPROVEN, stated plainly: not yet run on a booted Meta OS image, not wired as a systemd unit, never run inside a real operations room, host probes never yet run live.
parts.what: The patrol loop: reads the CISA known-exploited-vulnerabilities feed, checks each watched host's TLS certificate expiry, service liveness, and undeclared sensitive-port exposure; classifies every observation into the pack's six categories; appends one record per observation; yellow observations stop at record + flag, red observations run the escalation chain to a labelled SIMULATED endpoint only. Pure classification core plus CLI, no model calls, no changes to watched machines.

parts.proven: Driver pinning tests (tests/custos/test_driver.py): the STOP file halts before anything runs, a live lock blocks and a stale lock is stolen, a missing config is a logged no-op that never calls the patrol, a configured run invokes the patrol with the records and seen-state paths under the state dir, a patrol failure propagates its exit code. UNPROVEN, stated plainly: not yet run on a booted Meta OS image; the timer has never fired on real hardware.
parts.what: The standing service wiring (stage 2): the metaos-custos driver (kill switch, lock, config check, state layout) plus metaos-custos.service and metaos-custos.timer, installed by both image builds to /usr/local/bin with state at /var/lib/metaos/custos, the timer under relay.target, and the watched-host config read from /etc/metaos/custos.json.

summary: Night watch for machines: a patrol loop over real public signals (the CISA known-exploited-vulnerabilities feed, TLS certificate expiry, service liveness, undeclared sensitive-port exposure) that classifies what it actually observes into six machine-state categories and appends every observation to a patrol record. PARTIAL: the patrol loop runtime is built and pinning-tested, one live stage-1 feed patrol is committed under runs/, and stage 2 wires the patrol as a standing Meta OS service (driver, systemd timer, state root); it has not yet run on a booted Meta OS image and nothing here runs a real operations room.
summary_note: Observation aid only: it watches, classifies, and records. It never patches, restarts, reconfigures, or scans a host it was not given; it never invents an observation, and an escalation in stage 1 goes only to a labelled simulated endpoint, never to a real responder.

urgency.meaning: Red machine states: expired certificates, known-exploited vulnerabilities matching the inventory, services down, and their escalation summaries.
Yellow machine states: certificates expiring inside the warning window, anomalous exposure of undeclared sensitive ports.
Patrol completion summaries and baseline counts.

watchers.watches: Known-exploited vulnerabilities: which entries in the public feed name a vendor and product the installation's configured inventory declares. A match means the inventory names the product; it is an exposure record, not a claim that an exploit happened.

inputs: TLS handshake with each watched host
cert warning window from firstboot config
watchers.watches: Certificate expiry state per watched host: days remaining on the certificate the host actually presents, classified as baseline normal, expiring inside the warning window, or expired.

inputs: watched host list from firstboot config
watchers.watches: Service liveness and exposure: whether each watched host's service port answers, and whether any sensitive port answers that the installation did not declare expected for that host.
The patrol record: every observation the patrol made, its category and tier, and what the escalation chain did, kept in order as the checkable record of the watch.
